label: Analyst Notes
description: Unstructured overnight market commentary from the trading desk. The raw input the whole workflow starts from.

lesson.intent: Inspect where this raw note comes from, its real-world sources, and the access ingesting it would require.

labVersion: Local text fixture stored in lesson-intake.json (the note you read in the Intake task).
soloRebuildPath: Start with a local .txt fixture
Move to a watched folder where notes are dropped
Later replace with email or API ingestion
governanceNote: Ingesting from inbox, Teams, or a terminal needs access and permission; the original note's provenance must be retained for audit.
auditNote: As an inspection lesson it needs a clear 'what did you learn' beat, or a learner clicks past it.

label: Trader Flag
description: An escalation signal a trader raises when overnight movement may need a closer look.

lesson.intent: Interpret a human escalation signal and map it to the structured approvalRequired field the workflow acts on.

labVersion: Represented as the approval cue inside the analyst note fixture.
realWorldSources: A flag toggled in a trading tool
A verbal handoff captured on the desk
accessNeeded: Access to the trader's escalation channel
Agreement on what counts as a flag
soloRebuildPath: Add a simple boolean/flag field to your intake
Capture it manually at first
Later wire it to a chat or tool signal
governanceNote: Requires agreement on what counts as a flag, and ownership of the escalation channel.
auditNote: Overlaps the Intake build (the flag becomes approvalRequired there); clarify the distinct lesson so the two do not feel redundant.

label: Market Intake Record
description: A structured JSON record created from the analyst notes and trader flag. The first machine-readable artifact in the workflow.

lesson.intent: Extract hub, peakPrice, settledPrice, generationFlag, and approvalRequired from a messy note into valid JSON and pass field validation.

labVersion: Built by you in the Intake task by extracting fields from the analyst note.
accessNeeded: Agreement on the required intake fields
soloRebuildPath: Define the required JSON schema
Extract fields from local notes
Store the result as market-intake.json
Later automate extraction from email, Teams, or an API
governanceNote: Requires agreement on the required intake fields; the schema is the contract every downstream step trusts.
auditNote: Validation rules in src/lib/validators.js are frozen; any field change ripples to three downstream nodes.

label: Price Feed / CSV Rows
description: Raw overnight price rows for the relevant hubs, usually delivered as CSV or a market feed.

lesson.intent: Inspect where numeric data enters, its column format, and the access a real feed or export would require.

labVersion: Not wired up yet - shown to reveal where numeric data enters the workflow.
realWorldSources: A CSV export from a market system
accessNeeded: Access to the price feed or export
soloRebuildPath: Start with a local sample CSV
Parse it with a small script
Later subscribe to a real feed or API
governanceNote: Needs access to the feed or export and knowledge of the column contract.
auditNote: No local fixture exists yet, so the inspection lesson has little to examine; add a small sample CSV.

label: Forecast Data
description: Expected generation and price forecasts used to judge how the actual overnight numbers compare.

lesson.intent: Inspect a second numeric input and judge why 'which forecast is authoritative' matters before it is compared.

labVersion: Not wired up yet - shown as a second numeric input.
accessNeeded: Agreement on which forecast is authoritative
soloRebuildPath: Start with a static forecast file
Join it to the actuals by key
Later pull live forecasts on a schedule
governanceNote: Requires agreement on which forecast is authoritative (ownership of source-of-truth).
auditNote: Feeds only Variance Check, a later transformation, so this sub-branch stays dormant until Phase 3 lands.

label: Prior Day Reference
description: Yesterday's normalized prices, kept as a baseline so today's movement has something to compare against.

lesson.intent: Inspect how a saved prior run is retained and reused as today's comparison baseline.

accessNeeded: A retention location for past outputs
soloRebuildPath: Save each day's clean prices to a dated file
Load the previous file as a baseline
Later move to a small historical store
governanceNote: Needs read access to prior runs and a retention location; retention policy is a governance decision.
auditNote: Temporal cycle: depends on Distribution/Archive at the end of the workflow; confirm the UI does not render this as a confusing backward edge.

label: Clean Price Data
description: Normalized, validated price values pulled into a consistent table the rules engine can trust.

lesson.intent: Coerce and validate raw price rows into a trusted, normalized clean-prices.json table.

labVersion: Built by you in the Clean Price Data task by normalizing messy price rows into a numeric table.
realWorldSources: A transformation step in a script or notebook
A cleaned table in a database or warehouse
accessNeeded: Read access to the price feed
A place to store the cleaned table
soloRebuildPath: Read the raw price rows
Coerce and validate numeric fields
Emit a clean price table
governanceNote: Read access to the feed plus a store for the cleaned table; data-quality rules are the trust boundary for everything downstream.
auditNote: Recommended next interactive build: smallest, most self-contained transformation lesson and reuses the Intake JSON/validation concepts.

label: Threshold Policy
description: Reusable business rules that define when market movement requires attention. Referenced by several downstream steps.

lesson.intent: Set and version the threshold values reused by three downstream nodes, and decide their ownership and approval path.

labVersion: Built by you in the Threshold Policy task by setting and versioning the threshold values.
soloRebuildPath: Start with a local JSON rules file
Version it alongside the workflow
Later replace with a governed policy source
governanceNote: Strongest governance node on the map: needs business-owner approval, risk-policy access, and versioning. Reused by three downstream steps.
auditNote: Best candidate to deliver the doctrine-required governance moment; author as a short 'set and version a threshold' lesson.

label: Variance Check
description: Compares actuals against forecast and the prior day to surface meaningful variance before the risk rules run.

lesson.intent: Compute actual-vs-forecast and actual-vs-prior deltas and flag material variance.

labVersion: Built by you in the Variance Check task by computing actual-vs-forecast and actual-vs-prior deltas and flagging material variance.
accessNeeded: Access to forecast and prior-day data
Agreement on what variance is material
soloRebuildPath: Subtract forecast from actual per field
Flag values over a variance threshold
Pass the result into evaluation
governanceNote: Requires agreement on what variance is material (a business rule overlapping Threshold Policy).
auditNote: Stores an explicit variance-summary.json so Risk Evaluation consumes a derived, auditable signal instead of recomputing deltas.

label: Risk Evaluation
description: Applies the threshold policy to the intake record, clean prices, and variance to produce a decision-ready risk view.

lesson.intent: Apply the threshold policy to the intake record, clean prices, and variance to emit the reusable risk-evaluation.json record.

labVersion: Built by you in the Risk Evaluation task by applying the governed thresholds to today's day-over-day moves.
realWorldSources: A risk engine or policy service
accessNeeded: Read access to the upstream artifacts
soloRebuildPath: Load the intake record, clean prices, and policy
Apply the threshold rules
Emit a risk-evaluation record
governanceNote: Needs the agreed threshold values and read access to four upstream artifacts; the risk record should be auditable.
auditNote: Typed process but emits risk-evaluation.json; eventually split into Evaluate Risk (action) and Risk Evaluation Record (artifact). Highest fan-in (4 deps), so it sequences late.

label: Approval Template
description: A reusable template that shapes how an approval request is written when sign-off is needed.

lesson.intent: Define the reusable approval format and the required fields a sign-off request must contain.

labVersion: Built by you in the Approval Template task by recording the desk's agreed request format as a versioned template.
realWorldSources: A saved email or form template
soloRebuildPath: Start with a local Markdown/JSON template
Fill it from the risk evaluation
Later wire it to a real approval channel
governanceNote: Needs agreement on required approval fields; the template standardizes what every approver sees.
auditNote: Could become interpretation instead of governance if the authored lesson has the learner read/apply a template rather than define one.

label: Approval Decision
description: The branch point: does this movement require sign-off, or can it flow straight to the brief as routine?

lesson.intent: Encode the if/else branch from the risk evaluation and log each decision for audit.

labVersion: Built by you in the Approval Decision task by routing three mornings through the escalation fork and logging each decision.
realWorldSources: A human judgment call on the desk
soloRebuildPath: Encode the if/else from the risk evaluation
Make the threshold configurable
Log every decision for audit
governanceNote: Needs the escalation threshold and knowledge of who can approve; every decision should be logged for audit.
auditNote: The only true fork (two downstream branches); the decision log is now persisted as decision-log.json for audit.

label: Approval Route
description: When sign-off is needed, the request is routed to an approver and the response is captured before the brief goes out.

lesson.intent: Route a sign-off request to an approver and capture the yes/no response as approval-route.json.

labVersion: Built by you in the Approval Route task by capturing the Desk Manager's chat response as a structured approval record.
realWorldSources: An email or Teams approval request
accessNeeded: A place to record the response
soloRebuildPath: Write an approval request to a file
Capture a manual yes/no response
Later wire to email or a chat approval
governanceNote: Needs the ability to message the approver and a place to record the response; the response is an audit record.
auditNote: Emits approval-route.json but typed handoff (action yielding an artifact); real-world messaging integrations are out of MVP scope.

label: Routine Update Path
description: The other side of the branch: when no approval is needed, movement is logged as a routine note for the brief.

lesson.intent: Handle the no-approval branch: write a routine note when below threshold and keep it for the audit trail.

labVersion: Built by you in the Routine Update Path task by writing the system-authored log entry for a quiet morning.
realWorldSources: A no-action note on the desk
accessNeeded: A place to record routine outcomes
soloRebuildPath: Write a routine note when below threshold
Include it in the brief as context
Keep it for the audit trail
governanceNote: Needs a place to record routine outcomes; 'no action' must still be auditable.
auditNote: The quiet branch, easy to under-teach; its value is that the non-escalation path is still logged as routine-log.json.

label: Prior Day Brief Template
description: The brief's reusable structure, carried over from prior days so the morning output stays consistent.

lesson.intent: Inspect the reusable brief structure and how it keeps the daily output consistent before assembly.

soloRebuildPath: Save the brief layout as a template file
Fill it from upstream artifacts
Version it alongside the workflow
governanceNote: Needs agreement on the brief sections; template versioning keeps output consistent.
auditNote: Overlaps Prior Day Reference (structure vs baseline data); inspection may be too passive - consider interpretation when authoring.

label: Morning Brief
description: The approval-ready 7:00 AM summary that joins intake, clean prices, risk, and approval status into one business output.

lesson.intent: Assemble the intake record, clean prices, risk, approval status, and template into one approval-ready market-brief.md.

labVersion: Built in a future phase - shown to reveal the full workflow shape.
realWorldSources: A generated Markdown or PDF document
accessNeeded: Read access to all upstream artifacts
soloRebuildPath: Load the upstream artifacts
Fill the brief template
Render to Markdown
Later automate delivery on a schedule
governanceNote: Needs read access to all upstream artifacts plus the template; the assembled brief is the record of the day.
auditNote: Highest fan-in (7 deps); the natural capstone but requires nearly the whole graph first, so it is last in build order.

label: Distribution / Archive
description: The finished brief is delivered to the desk and stored for the record, seeding tomorrow's prior-day reference.

lesson.intent: Deliver the brief to the desk, archive it for the record, and seed tomorrow's prior-day baseline.

labVersion: Built by you in the Distribution / Archive task by recording the delivery, retention, and tomorrow-seeding run record.
realWorldSources: A shared drive or document store
accessNeeded: Send permission to the distribution list
Write access to the archive location
soloRebuildPath: Save the brief to a dated folder
Add a send step (email or chat)
Feed it back as tomorrow's prior-day reference
governanceNote: Needs send permission to the distribution list and write access to the archive; retention/audit policy applies.
auditNote: Action+thing ambiguity; recommend splitting into Distribution (handoff/action) and Archive (output/thing). Likely the first map shape change after the audit.
